description: XTREME-S is a benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains, and 4 task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval. It includes datasets such as Fleurs, MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, and Minds-14, and aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation and catalyze research in universal speech representation learning.

rai:annotationsPerItem: Between 1 and 3 recordings per sentence (2.3 on average) for the Fleurs component.
rai:dataBiases: There is a significant performance gap between Western European languages and other language groups (e.g., Sub-Saharan African, South Asian), partly due to larger amounts of unlabeled data available for Western European languages. The benchmark acknowledges that reducing gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction. Speech classification tasks are also prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels.
rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S aggregates several existing multilingual speech datasets (MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) and introduces a new dataset called Fleurs. Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark, using 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets in 102 languages, with between one and three recordings collected per sentence (2.3 on average), and new train-dev-test splits built with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences respectively.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a second version of the dataset, such as missing recordings or replaced low-quality recordings.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark aggregates multiple existing speech datasets: Fleurs (based on FLoRes MT benchmark sentences), MLS (derived from Librivox audiobooks), VoxPopuli (European Parliament sessions), CoVoST-2 (speech translation corpus), and Minds-14 (e-banking spoken intent data). Fleurs uses 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Results are much better on Western European languages than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African or South Asian languages, partly due to larger amounts of unlabeled data in Western European languages. The benchmark focuses on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects relevant to speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. FLEURS is complete at more than 97%, with some missing or low-quality recordings.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For MLS, the official 10-hour splits provided by the original authors are used to evaluate few-shot learning capabilities. For VoxPopuli, the 14 languages with more than 10 hours of data from the ASR task are selected. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets are merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits are built with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences respectively, with speakers of the train sets different from speakers in dev/test sets.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Updates will be made on the HuggingFace platform. A second version of the Fleurs dataset is anticipated with fixes for missing or low-quality recordings. Additional test sets may be added in the future to confirm the generalization ability of submissions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: XTREME-S aims to make speech technology available in all languages, which is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.
rai:dataUseCases: XTREME-S is intended for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations, benchmarking multilingual speech models on tasks including speech recognition, speech-to-text translation, speech classification (language identification and intent classification), and speech retrieval across 102 languages. It is also intended to catalyze research in data-efficient self-supervised speech representation learning for low-resource languages.

evidence.description: XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation, as well as catalyze research in "universal" speech representation learning.

evidence.rai:dataCollection: Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark. We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets, in 102 languages. We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence (2:3 on average), and build new train-dev-test splits with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: XTREME-S builds on top of the XTREME series of evaluation benchmarks for text understanding. Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark. We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets, in 102 languages. We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark. We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets, in 102 languages. The Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) dataset is a large corpus derived from read audiobooks of Librivox. VoxPopuli is a multilingual speech dataset for semi-supervised learning. It contains 400k hours of unannotated speech as well as speech transcriptions and translations.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The task consists of the official 10-hour splits provided by [6] to evaluate few-shot learning capabilities. We use the 14 languages with more than 10 hours of data from the ASR task. We merge monolingual datasets into a single multilingual dataset, with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation, as well as catalyze research in "universal" speech representation learning. XTREME-S strongly encourages data-efficient self-supervised representation learning.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: We note that the tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. We observe in Table 4 that results are much better on the Western European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction for future work building on XTREME-S. In general, speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels.

Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on our platform. We expect average results not to change significantly.
